raw_segments.text: In a government where numerous and extensive prerogatives are placed in the hands of an
hereditary monarch, the executive department is very justly regarded as the source of danger
and watched with all the jealousy which a zeal for liberty ought to inspire.
In a democracy where a multitude of people exercise in person the legislative functions
and are continually exposed by their incapacity for regular deliberation and concerted measures
to the ambitious intrigues of their executive magistrates, tyranny may well be apprehended
on some favorable emergency to start up in the same quarter.
But in a representative republic where the executive magistracy is carefully limited,
both in the extent and the duration of its power, and where the legislative power is
exercised by an assembly which is inspired by a supposed influence over the people with
an intrepid confidence in its own strength, which is sufficiently numerous to feel all
the passions which actuate a multitude, yet not so numerous as to be incapable of pursuing
the objects of its passions by means which reason prescribes.
It is against the enterprising ambition of this department that the people ought to indulge
all their jealousy and exhaust all their precautions.
